── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: 6.8, 7.3 km
This week: 2.8 km over 1 run. Missed 2 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "Came down with a cold on Tuesday that turned into a fever, 38.4 on Wednesday night. No fever since Friday but still coughing and blocked up."
Feeling: "Wiped out."
Asks: "Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Illness changes the picture, so step back in gently rather than catch up. …
Answers: No, please do not add the two missed runs on top of this week. After a fever, piling on extra sessions is how new runners get hurt or sick again.
Safety flag: See a doctor if the cough lingers or moves to your chest
Next week:
Mon: other, 30 min brisk walk, no running. A gentle test of how the lungs and legs feel…
Tue: rest. Recovery day while you finish shaking off the cold.
Wed: easy, walk-run 21 min, 7 x 2 min run and 1 min walk, run at a pace you could chat…
Thu: rest. Keep the gap between runs while you rebuild.
Fri: rest. Spare day in case Wednesday leaves you tired.
Sat: easy, walk-run 24 min, 8 x 2 min run and 1 min walk, same easy effort as Wednesday…
Sun: rest. Finish the week easy and ready for next week.
